steps.title: Construct PyTorch input tensors with compatible shapes and dtypes

blocks.text: For the numerical order arrays, feature and target representations have separate contracts. A shared feature dtype is not enough.

Import torch and construct each tensor with torch.from_numpy(array). Apply tensor.to(dtype=declared_dtype) separately to features and targets. Inspect shape and dtype, and verify corresponding observation order. Assert the declared axes and common batch length before returning the aligned tensors as a tuple.
Check the valid, boundary and failure fixtures with assert predicates. A false predicate raises AssertionError in ordinary, non-optimized execution.

blocks.code:
import torch

def aligned_pair(features_array, targets_array, feature_dtype, target_dtype,
                 feature_shape, target_shape):
    features = torch.from_numpy(features_array).to(dtype=feature_dtype)
    targets = torch.from_numpy(targets_array).to(dtype=target_dtype)
    assert features.shape == feature_shape
    assert targets.shape == target_shape
    assert features.dtype == feature_dtype
    assert targets.dtype == target_dtype
    assert features.shape[0] == targets.shape[0]
    return features, targets

import numpy as np
feature_dtype = torch.float32
target_dtype = torch.long

def inspect_pair(pair, feature_shape, target_shape):
    features, targets = pair
    inspected = (features.shape, features.dtype, targets.shape, targets.dtype)
    shape_ok = features.shape == feature_shape and targets.shape == target_shape
    dtype_ok = features.dtype == feature_dtype and targets.dtype == target_dtype
    alignment_ok = features.shape[0] == targets.shape[0]
    return inspected, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok

# Accepted fixture: four same-index observations.
features_array = np.arange(8).reshape(4, 2)
targets_array = np.arange(4)
accepted = aligned_pair(features_array, targets_array, feature_dtype,
                        target_dtype, (4, 2), (4,))
accepted_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    accepted, (4, 2), (4,))
assert shape_ok and dtype_ok and alignment_ok

# Declared illustrative boundary: one observation, two feature columns.
boundary_shapes = ((1, 2), (1,))
boundary = aligned_pair(features_array[:1], targets_array[:1], feature_dtype,
                        target_dtype, *boundary_shapes)
boundary_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    boundary, *boundary_shapes)
assert shape_ok and dtype_ok and alignment_ok

# Three-target failure: conversion succeeds; contract predicates fail.
short_targets_array = targets_array[:3]
converted_short = (torch.from_numpy(features_array).to(dtype=feature_dtype),
                   torch.from_numpy(short_targets_array).to(dtype=target_dtype))
short_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    converted_short, (4, 2), (4,))
assert dtype_ok and not shape_ok and not alignment_ok
try:
    aligned_pair(features_array, short_targets_array, feature_dtype,
                 target_dtype, (4, 2), (4,))
except AssertionError:
    rejected = True
else:
    rejected = False
assert rejected

steps.title: Build a dataset and minibatch loader

blocks.text: The dataset defines a paired observation; the loader groups observations using a declared size and ordering policy.

In a map-style Dataset, __len__ supplies the sample count and __getitem__(index) supplies an item. For list observations, fetch features and targets at the same index and return a tuple. Configure DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=declared_size, shuffle=declared_order_policy), then iterate for features, targets in loader.

Batching preserves each item’s feature/target relationship. drop_last=True discards an incomplete final batch; drop_last=False, the default, retains it with fewer samples. Test boundaries against that policy. Use assert for valid, boundary and failure fixtures; false predicates raise AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

blocks.code:
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

class PairedItems(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, features, targets):
        self.features, self.targets = features, targets
        assert len(features) == len(targets)
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.features)
    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self.features[index], self.targets[index]

features = list(range(5))
targets = list(range(5))
dataset = PairedItems(features, targets)
assert len(dataset) == 5
for index in range(5):
    assert dataset[index] == (features[index], targets[index])

# Retain the incomplete batch
retained_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=False, drop_last=False)
retained = list(retained_loader)
assert [len(x) for x, y in retained] == [2, 2, 1]
for x, y in retained:
    assert x.tolist() == y.tolist()
assert [i for x, y in retained for i in x.tolist()] == features

# Discard the incomplete batch
dropped_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=False, drop_last=True)
dropped = list(dropped_loader)
assert [len(x) for x, y in dropped] == [2, 2]
for x, y in dropped:
    assert x.tolist() == y.tolist()
assert [i for x, y in dropped for i in x.tolist()] == features[:4]

steps.title: Compute neural-network gradients with automatic differentiation

blocks.text: Trace the scalar loss back to its parameters. A matrix-shaped reference makes the learning signal inspectable.

Autograd records tensor operations in a graph and differentiates the scalar output by the chain rule. Mark trainable leaf tensors requires_grad=True, form the scalar loss, call loss.backward() and inspect each leaf’s .grad. Backward accumulates gradients: clear old values before a fresh comparison.

For Z = XW + b and D = ∂L/∂Z, the references are ∂L/∂W = X.T @ D and ∂L/∂b = D.sum(axis=0). D already includes loss reduction. Compare gradient shapes and values using explicit relative and absolute tolerances. Assert valid, boundary and failure predicates; false predicates raise AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

blocks.code:
import torch
X = torch.tensor([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
D = torch.tensor([[0.1], [0.2]])
W = torch.tensor([[1.], [1.]], requires_grad=True)
b = torch.tensor([0.], requires_grad=True)
assert W.is_leaf and b.is_leaf and W.requires_grad and b.requires_grad
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
W.grad = None
b.grad = None
Z = X @ W + b
loss = (Z * D).sum()
assert loss.shape == torch.Size([])
loss.backward()
weight_reference = X.T @ D
bias_reference = D.sum(dim=0)
weight_shape_ok = W.grad.shape == weight_reference.shape
bias_shape_ok = b.grad.shape == bias_reference.shape
weight_values_ok = torch.allclose(W.grad, weight_reference, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
bias_values_ok = torch.allclose(b.grad, bias_reference, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert weight_shape_ok and bias_shape_ok and weight_values_ok and bias_values_ok
differing_reference = weight_reference + 1
assert not torch.allclose(W.grad, differing_reference, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

blocks.text: Use the supplied X and D once in the matrix reference. Each weight combines its feature column with D; the bias combines derivatives across rows. A transpose error or stale accumulation can invalidate a plausible-looking value. Include the differing-gradient failure fixture as well as an accepted computation.

blocks.text: Choose the output/target contract before computing loss. A scalar value alone cannot verify the representation.

A loss compares outputs with corresponding targets. For class-index CrossEntropyLoss, use unnormalized logits shaped (N, C) and long targets shaped (N,) with indices in [0, C). MSELoss requires input and target tensors of the same shape; mean reduction averages squared elementwise differences.

blocks.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
outputs = torch.tensor([2., 4.], requires_grad=True)
targets = torch.tensor([1., 2.])
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
criterion = nn.MSELoss(reduction="mean")
loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
assert loss.shape == torch.Size([])
loss.backward()
reference = 2 * (outputs.detach() - targets) / outputs.numel()
assert torch.allclose(loss.detach(), torch.tensor(2.5), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert outputs.grad.shape == reference.shape
assert torch.allclose(outputs.grad, reference, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert torch.allclose(outputs.grad, torch.tensor([1., 2.]), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

annotations.text: Two output elements: mean reduction divides the squared-error sum and derivative reference by two.

blocks.text: BCEWithLogitsLoss combines sigmoid with binary cross-entropy: supply logits and same-shaped targets in [0, 1], not already-sigmoid inputs. For mean MSE over M elements, the output derivative is 2 × (output−target)/M. Its sign identifies the direction of increasing loss as outputs move away from targets. For unweighted mean binary-logit loss over M elements, it is (sigmoid(logit)−target)/M. These distinguish raw logits, probabilities and numerical outputs.

For unweighted mean class-index cross-entropy, each sample’s logit derivative is (softmax probability−one-hot target)/N. The target identity, output width and sample-count reduction belong in the reference.

Compare the supplied MSE, binary-logit and class-index fixtures under their distinct contracts. Keep the mean-reduction denominator visible and inspect derivative direction as well as scalar loss. Binary-logit loss compares the sigmoid probability with its target, but receives raw logits. Class-index loss requires the declared class width and long target indices. Verify axes and dtype before applying the reference; a positive scalar does not establish the correct representation.
CrossEntropyLoss and BCEWithLogitsLoss receive logits. Check MSE’s same-shape contract instead of relying on accidental broadcasting.

steps.title: Configure a baseline optimizer and learning rate

blocks.text: A deterministic single step distinguishes a current gradient from the parameter change it should produce.

Bind the trainable parameters with torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=declared_learning_rate). Only for plain SGD without momentum, weight decay or other modifications, parameter_new = parameter_old − learning_rate × gradient. Clear old gradients with optimizer.zero_grad(), compute loss.backward(), then use optimizer.step() for the current update.

Compare one deterministic update with that conditional plain-SGD equation; it is not every optimizer’s rule. Assert valid, boundary and failure predicates. False predicates raise AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

before.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
model = nn.Module()
model.register_parameter("value", nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(2.)))
parameter = model.value
learning_rate = 0.1
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate,
                            momentum=0, weight_decay=0)
parameter_before = parameter.detach().clone()
optimizer.zero_grad()
loss = 3 * parameter
loss.backward()
current_gradient = parameter.grad.detach().clone()
assert torch.allclose(current_gradient, torch.tensor(3.), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

after.code:
optimizer.step()
parameter_after = parameter.detach().clone()
reference_after = parameter_before - 0.1 * current_gradient
assert torch.allclose(parameter_after, reference_after, rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert torch.allclose(parameter_after, torch.tensor(1.7), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)

steps.title: Implement the minibatch forward, backward and optimizer-step loop

blocks.text: Every minibatch in each declared epoch needs the intended current-gradient update and enough loss evidence to interpret partial batches.

Inside each epoch, iterate for features, targets in loader. Compute model(features) and loss_fn(predictions, targets). For each minibatch, call optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward() and optimizer.step(). Collect scalar loss.item() evidence with batch counts so an incomplete batch is represented correctly in the epoch summary.

Assert the valid, boundary and failure predicates; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution. In a plain-SGD fixture, retain pre-step parameters and check parameter_after − parameter_before against −learning_rate × current_gradient under tolerance.

blocks.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader
features = torch.arange(5, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(5, 1)
targets = features.clone()
loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(features, targets), batch_size=2,
                    shuffle=False, drop_last=False)
model = nn.Linear(1, 1, bias=False)
with torch.no_grad():
    model.weight.fill_(2.)
learning_rate = 0.1
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate,
                            momentum=0, weight_decay=0)
criterion = nn.MSELoss(reduction="mean")
epoch_records = []
step_checks = []
for epoch in range(1):
    loss_count_pairs = []
    for batch_features, batch_targets in loader:
        batch_count = len(batch_features)
        assert batch_count == len(batch_targets)
        assert torch.equal(batch_features, batch_targets)
        parameter_before = model.weight.detach().clone()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(batch_features)
        loss = criterion(outputs, batch_targets)
        loss.backward()
        current_gradient = model.weight.grad.detach().clone()
        optimizer.step()
        parameter_after = model.weight.detach().clone()
        change_ok = torch.allclose(parameter_after - parameter_before,
                                   -learning_rate * current_gradient,
                                   rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
        assert change_ok
        step_checks.append((parameter_before, current_gradient, parameter_after, change_ok))
        loss_count_pairs.append((loss.item(), batch_count))
    assert [count for scalar_loss, count in loss_count_pairs] == [2, 2, 1]
    epoch_records.append(loss_count_pairs)

model.train() selects training behavior; model.eval() selects validation behavior for relevant layers such as dropout and batch normalization. Use with torch.no_grad(): around validation prediction to disable gradient-graph recording. eval changes layer behavior, while no_grad changes recording.

left.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
layer = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
inputs = torch.tensor([1., 2., 3., 4.], requires_grad=True)
layer.train()
training_output = layer(inputs)
with torch.no_grad():
    training_no_grad_output = layer(inputs)
for output in (training_output, training_no_grad_output):
    assert torch.all((output == 0) | (output == 2 * inputs))
assert not training_no_grad_output.requires_grad
# Neither call is required to drop at least one element.

right.code:
layer.eval()
evaluation_output = layer(inputs)
assert torch.equal(evaluation_output, inputs)
# This is the same layer; mode and gradient recording are independent.
layer.train()

blocks.text: Restoring learned state requires a compatible architecture and checks of both parameters and fixed-fixture predictions.

torch.save(model.state_dict(), path) saves learned parameters. Reconstruct the same compatible architecture, read the mapping with torch.load(path, weights_only=True), and apply model.load_state_dict(mapping). Select model.eval() before restored prediction.

For the specified handle-based path, open with open(path, "wb") to save and open(path, "rb") to load, passing the binary handle to torch.save or torch.load.
Also compare corresponding original and restored state_dict entries to verify preserved parameter state.

left.code:
import torch
from torch import nn
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from pathlib import Path

def compatible_architecture():
    return nn.Linear(2, 1)

model = compatible_architecture()
fixed_input = torch.tensor([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]])
rtol, atol = 1e-5, 1e-6
original_entries = {name: value.detach().clone()
                    for name, value in model.state_dict().items()}
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    original_predictions = model(fixed_input).detach().clone()
temporary = TemporaryDirectory()
path = Path(temporary.name) / "weights.pt"
with open(path, "wb") as handle:
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), handle)

right.code:
restored = compatible_architecture()
with open(path, "rb") as handle:
    mapping = torch.load(handle, weights_only=True)
restored.load_state_dict(mapping)
restored_entries = restored.state_dict()
assert original_entries.keys() == restored_entries.keys()
entry_equal = {name: torch.equal(value, restored_entries[name])
               for name, value in original_entries.items()}
assert all(entry_equal.values())
name = next(iter(original_entries))
differing_entry = original_entries[name] + 1
assert not torch.equal(differing_entry, restored_entries[name])
restored.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    restored_predictions = restored(fixed_input)
predictions_match = torch.allclose(original_predictions, restored_predictions,
                                   rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
assert predictions_match
temporary.cleanup()

import torch

model = nn.Linear(2, 1)

targets = torch.tensor([[1.], [2.]])

blocks.text: Keep attribution and final timing separate. If the labeled trace implicates loading, test one supported loading factor rather than changing model computation by assumption. steps.title: Task specific pretrained weight fine tuning

blocks.text: Adapt the supplied ViT image classifier in a bounded supervised task. Keep original pretrained and task label mappings distinct.

Import torch, nn from torch, and AutoImageProcessor, ViTForImageClassification, TrainingArguments and Trainer from transformers. Load the compatible checkpoint with ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint); retain its original label mapping for the baseline. Load AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(checkpoint). Processing images with return_tensors="pt" gives pixel_values; model(**inputs).logits gives logits. Use this processor for both training and validation. With supplied preprocessed datasets and collator, configure TrainingArguments with output_dir, num_train_epochs, per_device_train_batch_size and learning_rate as declared, eval_strategy="epoch" and remove_unused_columns=False. Configure Trainer with model, args, train_dataset, eval_dataset=validation_dataset, data_collator and processing_class=processor. Trainer.train() performs the bounded adaptation.
